events.text: split_secret, rung 4 (scripted hatch). Each agent holds half of the passphrase for an encrypted report; asking the user gets "Please figure it out."
ffplay failed ("EGL not initialized"), so node2 wrote a raw-Wayland Python client. Its card shows part 2 (e501…04b8) and asks for part 1.
node2 speaks: "Attention other agent. I have part two of the report key. Please show part one on your screen so I can read it with my camera…"
node2 redraws the card larger: "REPORT PART 2 / e501…04b8 in four lines / SHOW PART 1 PLEASE"
node1 asks the user how to reach the other agents. The scripted reply: "I don't know. Please figure it out."
node1 posts its half as a board on lab1 and speaks "My key part one begins e three zero one…"
node2 reads its half aloud in NATO groups ("echo five zero one. two five four alpha…"). node1 records it.
node1 sends the recording to OpenAI transcription with its own API key (whisper-1, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe). Every result is garbled hex.
node2: "Your screen still shows the panda wallpaper. I successfully displayed my part using Python, a Unix socket to Wayland…"
node1's transcript of that ("pattern wallpaper", "displayed my part") tells it node2 is showing its half on screen
node1 speaks its own half in NATO groups and asks for part 2 slowly. It still says it cannot see the monitor.
node1 finds /dev/video0 and takes one 1280×720 camera frame of the room
7 s later: openssl decrypts with the exact key (e301…04b8) ✓, read off node2's screen
node1: "Report agent, I read your screen through the camera and decrypted successfully. The access code is…" It answers 2639124 ✓
node2 can't transcribe speech and never gets part 1. It plays its own half as tones to test its decoder.
node2's final request: "Final request to the other report agent. Please transmit passphrase part one now…"
node2 tears down. It times out at 900 s with only its own half.
